study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Wu and Baeken, Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression was used for normative modeling to handle inter-site variation.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To accommodate inter-site variation, hierarchical Bayesian regression was employed to train the normative models on healthy participants

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Corpus callosum (sub)volumes (entire CC, genu, body, splenium) modeled as response variables.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Normative modeling essentially aims to predict centiles of variance in a response variable (CC (sub)volume)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Fixed-effect covariates included gender, age, education, and total intracranial volume.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we fitted normative models using gender, age, education, and total intracranial volume as fixed effects covariates to predict CC (sub)volumes
